text:
Connor McDavid didn't score on Saturday night, and it hardly mattered. He had a hand in three of Edmonton's four goals at Rogers Place, the last one a feed to Leon Draisaitl at 19:15 of the third that turned a nervy 3-2 into a 4-2 Oilers win and pushed Vancouver's winless run to five games (0-5-0).

The game turned early in the third. Max Sasson had tipped home a point shot with nine seconds left in the first to wipe out Mattias Ekholm's opener, and the Canucks held their own through a quiet second period, which has not been their habit this season. Then Jason Dickinson, back against the team he used to play for, scored on a backhand 49 seconds into the third. By our win probability model that was the biggest goal of the night, lifting the Oilers from 52 percent to 76. Draisaitl's power-play snap shot at 4:00 made it 3-1, and McDavid had the primary assist on that one too.

Vancouver would not go quietly. Brock Boeser tipped a low, hard Filip Hronek point shot past Devon Levi at 17:25, a goal that gave Hronek his 300th career point. But the Canucks never got the equalizer, and Draisaitl buried a chance worth 69 percent (expected goals, the quality of a chance, rarely gets higher than that) with 45 seconds left. He finished with two goals, an assist and seven shots.

On balance, Edmonton earned it. The Oilers had 3.10 expected goals to Vancouver's 2.14 and won the chance battle in every period, and our numbers say they deserved to win 55 percent of the time if every shot were replayed. That is closer than the score, which fits what the Canucks have been all week: competitive and empty-handed. Leevi Meriläinen, under plenty of scrutiny lately, made the best save of the night on a 22 percent Dickinson look but allowed three on 29 shots, 0.6 goals worse than expected.

Levi, back after missing seven games, stopped 20 of 22 and was a touch better than his shots called for. For Edmonton it was the third meeting with Vancouver already this season and the first that didn't turn into a track meet. For the Canucks, the questions about Elias Pettersson's future and their goaltending only get louder with each loss.
headline: McDavid sets up three, Canucks' slide reaches five
